160-degrees: B.A.: humanities, social sciences, languages and interdisciplinary studies, built on a flexible multi-track of majors and minors, including minors in other faculties. From Fall 2025, new students must finish at least one Arts program.
B.S.W.: professional social work through the School of Social Work, three years or two for those who have a degree, covering knowledge, practice, policy and diversity.
B.Th.: through the School of Religious Studies, mainly for those preparing for ordained Christian ministry, or for academic interest.
B.A. & Sc.: an interdisciplinary degree combining programs from Arts and Science or joint ones, preparing you for jobs, professional programs like business, law and medicine, or graduate study.
160-degree-programs: Some programs (marked **) are run outside Arts: consult advisers in both faculties and follow the other faculty's registration and requirements.
161-b-a-joint-honours-programs: Combine two components and register for both, and see an adviser in each department about courses and any joint project. If one component is from Arts, no extra Minor is needed.
Accounting and Finance components combine only with Economics.
163-b-a-faculty-programs: Environment, with Bieler, integrates courses from Arts, Science and Agricultural and Environmental Sciences. Population and Global Health accepts students from 2026–2027; details to come.
163-other-degrees: Religious Studies (B.Th., 120 credits) and Social Work (three-year B.S.W., 90 credits) have their own admission; contact the schools.
163-diploma-program: Diploma in Environment, 30 credits, through Bieler, for holders of a B.Sc., B.A. or equivalent, all at McGill.
163-skill-development-courses: The Writing Centre offers credit and non-credit courses, Foundation-approved ones, and tutoring.
163-internships-field-studies-and-study-: Earn credits and experience through these; see the Study Abroad and Field Studies for Arts Students page.
163-study-away-and-field-studies-for-art: A term or two elsewhere needs Faculty approval first. Options: bilateral exchanges, Independent Study Abroad, IUT, online courses, Summer J'Explore.
Credit can be refused if not pre-approved, if the school or course doesn't meet policy, or for intermediary organizations or intensive and condensed programs.
163-field-study-courses-and-field-study-: See McGill Abroad or p. 1194. Coordinator: Internships and Field Studies Office, 646B-2001 McGill College, by appointment; or SOUSA, Dawson Hall, Room 405.
164-summer-studies-in-the-faculty-of-art: Special summer courses from Arts departments. The Class Schedule has all of them.
164-french-language-centre: FRSL courses have limited enrolment and mandatory placement tests, beginners included. Past students find their recommendation in myCourses and contact the Centre for a permit.
164-placement-tests: Dates are on the Centre's site. You get a permit at the test and may need to show earlier transcripts. No credit for equivalents already passed at CEGEP or another university.
164-mcgill-summer-studies-in-greece-mssg: A 3-credit course in Thessaloniki with Aristotle University, open to McGill and other accredited students.
164-summer-intensive-language-program: Intensive first-year Ancient Greek and Latin, one or both. Both equal two years of ancient languages in twelve weeks, readying you for intermediate courses in Fall. Useful before Classics, Religious Studies or Medieval Studies, or for graduate school in related fields.
164-browse-academic-units-and-programs: Since 1843, one of Canada's oldest faculties, with flexible programs. Also the B.S.W., B.Th. and Bieler's Diploma in Environment.
167-first-year-seminars: Not every seminar runs yearly; see the Class Schedule, and p. 158 for eligibility.
167-faculty-of-arts-internship-program: Credit for work in your field, open to U2 and U3 students, normally after 30 credits of a 90-credit program or 45 of a 96–120 one, with CGPA 2.7 and the department's permission.
At least 150 hours with an approved host and a major paper from an academic perspective.
167-about-anthropology: Similarity and diversity of human behaviour, social and cultural systems and change, from origins to today, focused on Archaeology and Socio-Cultural Anthropology.
Good for teaching, research, law, medicine, foreign service, community work, public administration and journalism. Honours and Joint Honours need a GPA of 3.50 after first year.
167-core-courses: 350-level courses on method and theory, more intensive and restricted to U2+ Anthropology students.
167-anthropology-minor-concentrations: 18 credits, useful for social services, multicultural settings, development, Indigenous history, museums, education and media. Register before your second year, with no overlap with another program. Can expand into the Major.
168-location: Leacock Building, Room 712, 855 Sherbrooke St. W. Administrative and Student Affairs Coordinator: Ms. Joanne Terrasi.
168-program-description: Human development and diversity through evolution, prehistoric archaeology and socio-cultural anthropology, broadly or focused. Can expand to the Major.
168-complementary-courses-18-credits: 6–9 credits at the 200 level; 9–12 at the 300–500 level, with only 3 at 400–500 and one Special Topic.
168-program-description-2: For those taking courses across sub-fields before specializing. No prerequisites. A quantitative methods course is encouraged but doesn't count.
168-degree-requirements-b-a-sc-students: Part of a B.A. & Sc.; you need both program and degree requirements. SOUSA's Degree Planning Guide helps, and fitting them is your responsibility.
168-core-350-level: Restricted to Anthropology program students with U2 standing or above.
169-undergraduate-level: 18 more credits, at most 6 at the 200 level.
169-program-description: More focus, breadth and depth, an asset for graduate or professional school.
169-complementary-courses-54-credits: Up to 9 credits at 300–400 from other departments, if related to your focus and approved by your adviser.
169-200-300-level: Up to 36 credits, at most 21 at 200 and 6 Special Topics.
169-400-500-level: At least 9 ANTH credits, at most 3 Special Topics.
169-program-description-2: Combine with any other Arts discipline. Consult an adviser in the other department, using a tracking form from Anthropology. Arrange the thesis with both, with a supervisor in each. Keep program GPA 3.50 and CGPA 3.00.
169-required-course-3-credits: The thesis is normally 6 credits, 3 for each component, set with advisers from both.
170-300-level: At least 6 ANTH credits, one Special Topic at most.
170-400-500-level: At least 6 ANTH credits, one 400-level Special Topic at most.
171-about-art-history-and-communication-: History of visual arts, material culture and architecture from antiquity to now, mainly Europe and North America, in cultural and social context. Offers a major, minor, honours and joint honours.
Communication Studies has a minor, and an M.A. and Ph.D.
171-orientation-session-for-new-students: New students must attend the Advising Fair, on the first business day after Undergraduate Orientation in late August or early September, then can book an adviser.
171-location: McCall MacBain Arts Building, Room 155, 853 Sherbrooke St. W.
171-program-description: An introduction to diverse artistic traditions from ancient to contemporary times, expandable to the Major.
171-complementary-courses-18-credits: 3–15 credits from the introductory list on methods and theories; 3–15 from departmental courses, at least 9 at 300+. No studio courses.
Architecture-related courses in the School of Architecture, East Asian Studies and Philosophy may count after consulting the Department.
172-program-description: A critical look at media and communication technologies in society: democracy and urban life, technology's social life, history of media, and how media represent social difference.
173-program-description: Analysis of visual and material culture from ancient to contemporary times, across fields and methods.
173-complementary-courses-36-credits: 3–15 credits from the intro list; 21–33 from departmental courses, at most 12 at 200 and at least 3 at 400+ (not ARTH 490). No studio courses; related architecture courses may count.
174-program-description: In-depth training in art historical methods and research, for graduate study and related careers. Apply after first year with 12+ Art History credits; competitive. Needs a program GPA of 3.50 on top of the 3.0 CGPA.
174-complementary-courses-48-credits: 3–15 credits from the intro list; 33–45 from departmental courses, at most 15 at 200, at least 6 at 400+ (not ARTH 490), and 6 in another language or related disciplines with written approval.
175-program-description: Flexible, with breadth, depth and research, for graduate study. Apply after first year with 12+ credits; competitive; program GPA 3.50 and CGPA 3.0.
175-complementary-courses-30-credits: 3–15 credits from the intro list; 15–27 from departmental courses, at most 12 at 200 and at least 3 at 400+ (not ARTH 490).
177-cognitive-science: Consider the Minor in Cognitive Science (p. 1165).
178-about-computer-science: See Science's section (p. 1167) for staff and details. You need MATH 133, 140, 141 or equivalents to start. Declare the Minor when registering in your second-last year.
178-joint-honours-in-mathematics-and-com: See p. 1210. Admission rests on strong CEGEP math. Consult an honours adviser in both departments. Keep CGPA and program GPA at 3.00.
178-main-office: McConnell Engineering Building, Room 318, 3480 University St.
178-program-description: The basics of computer science, alongside any Arts program.
178-required-courses-9-credits: If you've done the equivalent of COMP 202, take another complementary instead.
178-complementary-courses-9-15-credits: See an adviser about approved sequences. 6 credits from the first list; Advanced Standing means electives instead.
9 credits from the list or COMP at 300+, not COMP 396, 400, 401, 402 or 480.
179-program-description: Only for Major Concentration students in Computer Science or Software Engineering, with no overlap. Together they come close to Science's Major. Get courses approved by an adviser.
Two programs in one unit means a third elsewhere is needed to graduate.
179-complementary-courses-18-credits: COMP at 300+, not COMP 396. Up to 3 credits may be MATH from the list.
179-program-description-2: An in-depth introduction to computer science. With the Supplementary Minor, it comes close to Science's Major. Two programs in one unit means a third elsewhere is needed.
179-required-courses-18-credits: Finish MATH 133, 140, 141 or equivalents first. With programming knowledge, swap COMP 202 for a complementary.
